title: Continuous Noisy-Loop Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.24213v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Efficient learning and inference need not imply a compact probabilistic circuit. We quantify this distinction for continuous noisy readings of agreement between adjacent latent spins on a known square grid with $d$ edges. With known margins and bounded Lipschitz channels, minimax squared Hellinger risk is $\Theta(\min\{1,dN^{-2/3}\})$ from $N$ independent vectors, without a reliability lower bound. A spline estimator reaches this rate in polynomial arithmetic time given a fixed positive reliability bound; an exponential-size mixture removes that requirement. At fixed positive reliability, nonnegative decomposable circuits need $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt d))$ nodes for fixed total-variation error below one, even when each leaf uses at most $\alpha d$ coordinates, $0<\alpha<1$. Optimal Kullback--Leibler (KL) approximation error is $\Theta(d/\max\{\log d,\sqrt\ell\})$ in either direction with at most $d^r$ nodes and leaf scopes $\ell\leq\alpha d$,

translated_abstract: 高效的学习与推理并不必然意味着存在紧凑的概率电路表示。本文针对已知方形网格（含 $d$ 条边）上相邻潜在自旋之间一致性的连续含噪读数，量化了这一区别。在已知边际参数且有界 Lipschitz 信道的条件下，基于 $N$ 个独立观测向量，极小极大平方 Hellinger 风险为 $\Theta(\min\{1, dN^{-2/3}\})$，且该结果不依赖任何可靠性下界假设。在给定固定正的可靠性下界时，样条估计器可在多项式算术时间内达到该速率；而指数规模的混合模型则无需该假设。在固定正的可靠性条件下，即使每个叶子节点最多使用 $\alpha d$ 个坐标（$0<\alpha<1$），非负可分解电路仍需要 $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt d))$ 个节点才能将总变差误差固定地控制在 1 以下。在节点数至多 $d^r$、叶子作用域 $\ell\le\alpha d$ 的约束下，两个方向上的最优 Kullback–Leibler（KL）逼近误差均为 $\Theta(d/\max\{\log d, \sqrt\ell\})$。
tldr: 本文量化了“统计上高效可学”与“存在紧凑概率电路”之间的本质差距：对网格上相邻自旋一致性的连续含噪读数，样条估计器可在多项式时间内达到极小极大最优的 Hellinger 风险 $\Theta(\min\{1, dN^{-2/3}\})$，而紧凑的非负可分解电路则需 $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt d))$ 规模的节点，并给出了 KL 逼近误差的精确刻画。
en_tdlr: This paper quantifies the gap between statistically efficient learning and compact probabilistic circuit representation: for continuous noisy readings of adjacent-spin agreement on a grid, a spline estimator achieves the minimax-optimal squared Hellinger risk $\Theta(\min\{1, dN^{-2/3}\})$ in polynomial time, while nonnegative decomposable circuits require $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt d))$ nodes, with optimal KL approximation error $\Theta(d/\max\{\log d, \sqrt\ell\})$.
